georeference.projection: plate carree (equirectangular): column linear in longitude, row linear in latitude
georeference.pixel_centre_formula: lon = lon_left_edge + (col + 0.5) / 45; lat = lat_top_edge - (row + 0.5) / 45 (0-based col, row)

earthmaps_tile_origin.note: tile (0, 0) samples pixel (col wr, row hr); tile (x, y) at scale s samples pixel (x/s + wr, y/s + hr), worldgen.lua:221-224,244

georeference.status: derived: least-squares fit on the Atlantic raster (see atlantic.json georeference_fit) plus exact crop offsets; datum assumed WGS84

land_mask_rule: land = g m G d D s S (grass-1, grass-3, grass-2, dirt-3, dirt-6, sand-1, sand-3); water = o O w W. Rivers, lakes, marsh and the 1 px coastline stroke are all water classes in the data, so they count as water. No shallow-water class exists.
coast_definition: land pixels 4-adjacent to a water pixel inside the raster (the raster border is not water)

diagonal_only_links.definition: 2x2 blocks with water on one diagonal and land on the other: water joins only in 8-connectivity, and land likewise

lakes_4conn.definition: water components (4-connected) that do not touch the raster border

thin_water.definition: water pixels not covered by any all-water 3x3 square (morphological opening); width 1 = not covered by any all-water 2x2 square
thin_water.png: atlantic-thinwater.png (all thin water, not only components >= 20 px)

straits_and_isthmuses.method: inside the window only: seeds snapped to the nearest pixel of the right kind within 5 px; max_passable_*_square_px = largest k such that a k x k all-water (or all-land) square can move in 4-connected steps from a placement covering seed A to one covering seed B (0 = not connected)

cities.position_rule: tile = chunk centre of (position * 2 * scale), worldgen.lua:38-40; pixel = (2x + wr, 2y + hr)
cities.clash_effect: initCityChunks raises 'Chunk position already exists in chunk map' (worldgen.lua:80-81) when two cities share a chunk

list.full_name: North America, United States, El Paso
list.name: El Paso

river_sampler_simulation.method: numpy port of generateTileName (worldgen.lua:239-311), including the 4-corner weighted vote and random()/max_scale jitter (numpy RNG, seed 1, instead of Factorio's math.random); water = o O w W; connected_4 = the two river end points are joined by 4-connected water tiles inside the window

georeference_fit.method: least squares on extreme pixels of matched land components (4-connected), outliers dropped above max(3*MAD, 3 px); x and y fitted independently

snapped.model: integer crop (511 columns, 127 rows) of a 16200 x 8100 px, 45 px/deg global plate carree grid
